questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 21 days. B and C together can do it in 24 days. A and C together can do it in 33 days. In how many days approximately will A, B and C finish it together?

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 221 ÷ 2 = 110.5 units/day.

Time taken by A, B and C together = 1848 ÷ 110.5 ≈ 16.72 days.

Rounding off to the nearest integer, we get 17 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 days.**

Total Work Concept

Total work is universally considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given number of days. This prevents complicated fractions and keeps efficiency values as simple integers.

questions.question: A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days, while B alone can finish it in 25 days. How many days will A take to complete the same work alone?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Work done by A and B in 20 days

Work done by B alone in 25 days

**Concept:**

The difference of reciprocals of times taken by two entities working together and one entity alone gives the work rate of the other entity.

**Solution:**

Work rate of A and B together = 1/20

Work rate of B alone = 1/25

Work rate of A alone = (1/20) - (1/25) ⇒ 0.01

Time taken by A to complete the work alone = 1/0.01 ⇒ 100 days

**Therefore, A will take 100 days to complete the same work alone.**

questions.question: Three number are in the ratio of 4 ∶ 5 ∶ 6, and their LCM is 180. Their HCF is:

Let the common multiplier be x, which acts as the HCF of the numbers.

Given LCM = 180 ⇒ 60x = 180 ⇒ x = 3.

⇒ LCM of 4, 5, and 6 = 60

⇒ Therefore, the LCM of 4x, 5x, and 6x = 60x

⇒ We are given that their overall LCM is 180.

⇒ x = 180 ÷ 60

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their LCM and HCF. Formula: a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b). This rule does not directly extend to three numbers.

If the HCF of two or more numbers is 1, they are called co-prime numbers. For mutually co-prime numbers, their LCM is simply the product of the given numbers.

When numbers are expressed in their simplest simplified ratio, the common multiplier 'x' required to obtain the actual original numbers represents their Highest Common Factor (HCF).

questions.question: Find the compound interest on Rs. 3,00,000, compounded half-yearly, for 2(1)/(2) years at the rate of 20% per annum.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Half-yearly rate = 20% ÷ 2 = 10% (1/10) and Time = 2.5 × 2 = 5 cycles.

For 5 cycles, P = 10⁵ = 100000 units, A = 11⁵ = 161051 units.

Compound Interest (CI) = 161051 − 100000 = 61051 units.

Since P = 100000 units = Rs. 3,00,000, Total CI = 61051 × 3 = Rs. 1,83,153.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,83,153.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Principal (P) = Rs. 3,00,000

⇒ Rate of interest (R) = 20% per annum

⇒ Time (T) = 2.5 years

**Formula Used:**

⇒ A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5dfdcefdfa1e4503188153d36cb3e3121ce34446832030451b92d811ce875048.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Since interest is compounded half-yearly, Rate = 20% ÷ 2 = 10%

⇒ Number of conversion periods (n) = 2.5 × 2 = 5

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (1 + 10/100)⁵

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (11/10)⁵

⇒ A = 3,00,000 × (161051 / 100000)

⇒ A = 3 × 161051 = 4,83,153

⇒ Compound Interest (CI) = A − P

⇒ CI = 4,83,153 − 3,00,000 = 1,83,153

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,83,153.**

**__Additional Information__**

Half-yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the given annual rate is divided by 2, and the total time period in years is multiplied by 2.

Quarterly Compounding
